rows.grounds: compound of tat and kāryam, referring to the ritual act
locative indicating the locus of recollection
compound pūjā-phala with verb aśnute; fused form kept as one token

items.question: Does mere mental recollection of a ritual act secure the fruit of worship?
premises: A ritual act can be recalled in the mind.
Mental recollection alone does not constitute actual offering.
The fruit of worship depends on proper offering rather than mere recollection.
items.inference: Therefore, one who only remembers the ritual act in the mind does not attain the fruit of worship.
items.plain_english: Having remembered that act in the mind, one does not enjoy the fruit of worship.
